cultural.vision_reason: This is rock art—pecked petroglyphs of giraffes, oryx, Barbary sheep and other animals on a sandstone boulder—consistent with ancient rock art traditions of the Nile/Nubian desert region, made by an earlier culture no longer practiced. It is a documented archaeological feature of the region, plausible for the claimed ethnicity's homeland.

physical.title: digital photograph (colour)
physical.summary:
Digital photograph (colour); view of engraved rock art on a  sandstone boulder, showing the figures of Barbary sheep,   dogs,   giraffes, one cow, one ibex, oryx, gazelle, and six unidentified shapes.  All figures  are upright, pecked and more or less infilled.  The giraffes are  the largest figures, two of them dominating the upper right of  the tableau.  There appear to be two giraffes, both facing left, and an oryx with straight horns.  The other figure on the other side of the boulder is a quadruped with short legs, short body and long straight horns that go straight up (oryx?) To the upper right of this there  are two Barbary sheep figures, that on top facing left, the other  right, towards the figure of a dog with tail curved up, apparently  running towards them with limbs outstretched.  To the lower  right of this, below the large giraffe, is the apparent figure of a  Nubian ibex, with its distinctive large curved corrugated horn  viewed from side on, facing left.  Below this is are three Barbary sheep.  At the base is a Barbary sheep with large  horns with legs outstretched. Above it's back is a dog. Behind it another dog that is partly overlapped with a dog that faces the opposite direction - to the left is another barbary sheep with a crudely pecked dog behind it. The left half of the tableau, across a natural vertical  break in the rock, is dominated by five large, amorphous, heavily  pecked and infilled blotches.  A 5cm photo scale has been fitted  at the base of the image.  Wadi Hamra, Egypt.
